newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian govt ready to revise "Eurotax" details.
newsitem.headline: Italian govt ready to revise "Eurotax" details.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government said on Wednesday that it was willing to revise details of a controversial "Euro-tax" it plans to levy next year as long as the amount of revenue it is intended to raise was not reduced.

Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said the offer was intended as an olive branch to the centre-right Freedom Alliance, which has bitterly attacked the provisions and the overall shape of the government's austerity budget for 1997.
"We are ready to modify the Euro-tax if that can help improve relations with the opposition. The total should remain the same but we are ready to change the mix of the measure," Treu told reporters.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government has drawn up a tough budget for 1997 designed to cut 62.5 trillion lire ($41.3 billion) from next year's deficit to help Italy meet the conditions for membership of Europe's planned single currency.
A key element of the package is the Euro-tax, designed to raise 12.5 trillion lire through a mixture of a one-off levy on income tax and other fiscal measures.
The Euro-tax element was missing when the rest of the budget was approved by the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) this month in a vote boycotted by the opposition.
A deal on the measure was hammered out with trades unions last week and is due to be added to the budget in the form of an amendment, possibly later on Wednesday, in the Senate.
Treu's remarks followed a statement on Tuesday night from the Senate leader of the leftist PDS party in the government, Cesare Salvi, that Prodi's coalition was ready to bargain.

Treu said it was not certain how changes could be made but mentioned differences in Euro-tax levy thresholds for wage earners and the self-employed and tax on employees' severance payments as areas the government was looking at.
As now conceived, the income tax levy would kick in for the self-employed on income above 10 million lire and at above 23 million lire for wage earners.
The gulf has angered the centre-right Freedom Alliance, which has a large electoral base among the self-employed and wants the difference narrowed or removed.

However, political sources say such a concession to the opposition could confront Prodi with resistance from the hardline Communist Refoundation party, which ensures the government's majority in the lower house of parliament.

The party's lower house leader Oliviero Diliberto has said Communist Refoundation will ask for the wage earners' threshold to be raised to 30 million lire if the Euro-tax provision is amended for the self-employed.
